title: SA/100/2004 of U.P.F.C. Vs SMT. KULDAI NEGI

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Second Appeal No. 100 of 2004
Uttar Pradesh Financial Corporation .....Appellant
Versus
Smt. Kuldai Negi ....Respondent
Mr. Naresh Pant, Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, Senior Advocate assisted by Ms. Varsha Sharma, Advocate for the
respondent.

Dated: 17th December, 2018
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
 The appellant before this Court is a Statutory
Corporation created under the State Financial Corporation Act.
The appellant has agitated his grievance in the present Second
Appeal, being aggrieved against the judgment and decree dated
09.09.2004, as passed by the District Judge, Chamoli in Civil
Appeal No. 2 of 2004, Uttar Pradesh Financial Corporation Vs.
Smt. Kuldai Negi as well as the judgment of the learned Trial
Court dated 03.03.2004, i.e. Court of Civil Judge (Senior
Division), Chamoli, Gopeshwar, as rendered in Original Suit No. 2
of 2002, Smt. Kuldai Negi Vs. Uttar Pradesh Financial Corporation
Ltd., whereby, the suit for recovery of Rs.60,000/- was decreed
concurrently in favour of the plaintiff.

2. As per the plaint case, the plaintiff has taken financial
assistance from the appellant to the Second Appeal for
establishment of a Hotel called as "Hotel Mandhata". The
plaintiff's case was that for various reasons, she could not remit the
amount of installments due under the loan agreement, and thus,
was held to be a defaulter. For the purposes of taking benefit of
one time settlement, under the scheme floated by the Corporation
under the directives of Reserve Bank of India, a meeting was held

2
between the parties on 25.06.1996, when plaintiff is said to have
submitted a proposal. Her case is that in the proposal, thus
submitted by her on 25.06.1996, it was clearly mentioned that as
on the said date total loan liability payable by the plaintiff
respondent was calculated to be Rs.6,00,000/-. Her case in the suit
was that the amount of money deposited by her prior to it was to be
remitted back or adjusted against the total loan liability. The
details of payment which was sought to be adjusted was :-
1. 30.03.1996-Cheque-Rs.30,000/-received on 08.05.1996.
 2. 10.05.1996-Cash-Rs.40,000/-
3. It was further case that a settlement of one time was
received by her on 07.01.1997. As a consequence of one time
settlement on 28.06.1996, the appellant waived off Rs.1,24,233.22.
The plaintiff case was that she had made the deposit, but she
alleged that she was surprised to receive notice dated 29.05.1996
from the Regional Manager, raising a demand of balance amount
payable under the terms of one time settlement 28.06.1996.
Plaintiff's case was that after adjusting about amount paid prior to
one time settlement, nothing would be payable. But, still Financial
Corporation had issued a last and final letter for strict action by
letter 30.06.1998. She submits that she went to the office of the
Corporation on 22.09.1998 and learnt that deposit made by her
prior to one time settlement dated 28.06.1996 has not been
adjusted. But faced with the aforesaid situation, she submitted that
she has deposited Rs.38,000/- in the office of the appellants under
protest on 22.09.1998; 26.12.1998 and 21.01.1999, thus, in total
she was forced to deposit Rs.83,718/- under protest. After the
deposit made by the plaintiff, her case was that on 30.01.1999,
account was closed and the mortgage documents were returned to
her on 30.01.1999.
4. The plaintiff / respondent, herein, is said to have
instituted a suit on 31.01.2002, being a suit of recovery of a sum of

3
Rs.60,000/-, along with 18% interest, which she contended in the
suit was an amount which she has remitted back to the State
Financial Corporation in lieu of the loan advances to her by way of
financial assistance way back in the year 1979-83. Since, there
was a default committed by the plaintiff, the State Financial
Corporation had initiated the proceedings under Section 29 of the
State Financial Corporation Act and, on the issuance of the said
notice under Section 29 dated 26.08.1996, the plaintiff respondent
extended an offer for one time settlement and on 25.06.1996,
wherein, in the said offer, the total liability was held to be Rs.6 lacs
only, hence, the deposit of Rs.70,000/- already deposited was to be
adjusted and, thereafter, remaining amount was settled to be
deposited in 12 installments. The parties have entered into a one-time settlement on 28.06.1996. As a consequence of the one-time
settlement, the same was approved by the Financial Corporation on
the said day i.e. 30.01.1999, the documents which were deposited
in lieu of equitable mortgage created in favour of the Financial
Corporation too stood returned back to the principal borrower, i.e.
the defendant, herein.
5. In the suit, in question, the plaintiff's case was that as
soon as in lieu of the one-time settlement, the amount as settled has
been paid back, in that eventuality, the amount of money
amounting to Rs.60,000/- which has been deposited by the
borrower, plaintiff, with the Financial Corporation, ought to have
been remitted back because that amount will be treated as an
amount deposited in excess to the settled amount in pursuance to
the one time settlement.
6. Thus, in the plaint as filed on 31.01.2002, following
reliefs by way of decree of recovery was sought :

7. The proceedings of the suit was contested by the
Financial Corporation by filing their written statement on the
premise that the manner in which, the one time settlement dated
28th June, 1996 is being construed by the plaintiff is not an
appropriate interpretation for the reason being that the one time
settlement which happens to be flowing from the rights conferred
to them under Section 48, Sub-section 2 (c) (g) of the State
Financial Corporation Act, has got a statutory force when it
happens to be based on the policy decision taken by the Board in
the light of the circulars issued by the Reserve Bank of India from
time to time and, furthermore, the argument of the State Financial
Corporation before the Court below was that once the covenant of
the one time settlement was accepted by the plaintiff and she has
acted on it and she has taken the advantage of the settlement and
had remitted the amount as settled thereto, they could not have
reverted back and instituted the suit for recovery of the amount at a
belated stage as an afterthought on the premise that that was an
amount paid in excess to the amount settled in one-time settlement.
However, the suit proceeded, parties led their respective evidence,
the evidence of the defendant appellant was closed by the learned
Trial Court on 04.02.2004 due to their failure to adduce the
evidence at an appropriate time provided by the learned Trial
Court. The defendant appellant case in the written statement was
that as a consequence of one time settlement entered on
28.06.1996, total amount of Rs.6,00,000/- was payable by plaintiff
respondent in 12 equal installments, since it was paid as per
schedule, the amount of interest accrued on it and it became
payable by plaintiff / respondents. Further, the defendant /
appellant's case was that deposit alleged to be paid by plaintiff

5
prior to one time settlement was an amount paid prior to close of
financial year of 1995-96, hence, it cannot be adjusted. Thus, the
amount sought to be recovered from her by letter dated
29.05.1998, was the amount falling due to be paid due to non
compliance of the conditions of one time settlement.
8. On exchange of pleadings, following issues were
framed by the Trial Court :-

9. Admittedly, according to the counsel for the parties,
this closure of opportunity on 04.02.2004, to lead evidence of the
defendant / appellant has attained finality and the same has not
been challenged either in any independent proceedings before the
superior Court or by invoking Section 105 of the C.P.C. in the first
appeal preferred by the appellant, being aggrieved against the
judgment of the Trial Court dated 3rd March, 2004. Hence, having
failed to challenge the order, whereby, it was directed to close the
opportunity to lead evidence has attained the finality and a finding
has been recorded by the Trial Court that defendant / appellant has
not led any oral or documentary evidence, despite of various
opportunities given to them by the Trial Court.
10. What is more remarkable to observe in this case is
that the entire controversy is pertaining to the modalities settled
between the parties, as a consequence to one time settlement dated

6
28.06.1996, this document which was in the custody of defendant
appellant was rather never brought on record by either of the
parties so as to enable the Court to derive as to what were the
actual norms based on which the one time settlement has been
arrived at because for the purposes of considering the stand taken
by the defendant/appellant that the amount already deposited
would be exclusive of the amount settled by the one time
settlement, there has had to be determination of the one time
settlement dated 28th June, 1996, which was never placed on record
before the learned Trial Court or at least before the 1st Appellate
Court by invoking under Order 41 Rule 27 of the C.P.C. On that
premise, the learned Trial below on 03.03.2004 had decreed the
suit holding thereof that the amount deposited by the plaintiff
would be an amount in excess to the amount settled by the one
time settlement and, hence, the suit was decreed.
11. Trial Court, accordingly, in the judgment held as
under :-
1. Because in the offer 25.06.1996 given by the
plaintiff, the deposit was shown to be settled against the one
time settlement proposal. Court held that there is no proof
to the contrary that Financial Corporation has not accepted
this proposal of the plaintiff / respondent.
2. In the one time settlement, there was no condition
for payment of defaulted interest to be paid by the plaintiff.
Hence, there was no liability agreed to be settled to pay
default interest.
3. The Court held that the issue of as to whether
plaintiff failed to pay installments as scheduled, no evidence
was led by the defendant/appellant to the contrary.
12. Based on the aforesaid premise, the appellant
challenged the judgment of Trial Court dated 03.03.2004, by filing
a First Appeal under Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

13. Consequently, the Appeal too, by the impugned
judgment dated 09.09.2004 has been concurrently affirmed by the
judgment of the Trial Court holding thereof that the plaintiff would
be entitled to receive back the amount of Rs.70,000/- as paid by the
plaintiff in excess to the amount and the appeal was dismissed.
14. Having carefully gone through the judgment on record
and considering the fact that the defendant has to blame himself for
not diligently participating in the proceedings before Court below
because having not challenged the order of closure of his
opportunity dated 04.02.2004 to lead evidence and also because of
the fact that the defendant had to stand on his own leg by
producing the document relating to one time settlement, which was
not done by defendant / appellant at any stage of the proceedings
before the learned Trial Court or before the Appellate Court,
consequently, this Court holds that the Second Appeal is concluded
by the concurrent finding of fact which do not call for any
interference by this Court in the exercise of its power under 100
C.P.C.
15. However, at the time when the appeal was admitted
on 21.12.2004, this Court has framed the following substantial
questions of law:
"1. Whether, the trial court had jurisdiction to
interfere with the terms of the agreement entered into
between the parties ?
2. Whether, the amount deposited before one time
settlement could have been adjusted within the amount in
question ?"
16. This Court for the consideration made above is of the
considered view that after hearing the rival contention of parties at
length that none of the questions as framed by this Court at the
time of admission is involved for adjudication in the second

8
appeal, which is to be answered by this Court, for the reason
already stated above because it was an onus to prove the case in
favour which was to be discharged by the appellant herein because
appellant wanted to resist the claim of the plaintiff with regard to
the refund of the amount which the plaintiff contended to have
deposited in excess of the amount settled by the one time
settlement. It was defendant/appellant, who had to shoulder the
responsibility to advance the claim raised in the suit which the
Financial Corporation has failed to discharge even upto this
Second Appellate stage as no efforts was made by them to produce
the one time settlement, the document which was required to be
considered mainly to decide the case.
17. In that eventuality, once the benefit of the terms of
agreement or one time settlement has been sought to be derived by
the defendant / appellant in their favour before this Court, it was
his onus to place the one time settlement which was in their
custody on record to prove the same as to what extent the liability
has been settled in terms of the said one time settlement. The
consistent failure on the part of the appellant to place the said
document on record would render the question No. 1 as to be not
answerable in their favour since he has failed to discharge his
responsibility in the proceedings before the Court below and even
upto this second appeal.
18. The second question which has been framed for
determination pertaining to what amount of deposit was payable as
a consequence of one time settlement, yet again is a question
which is inter-related to substantial question number one, and
could only be flowing from a terms of one time settlement and
since the same has not been produced before the Court below and
not even at the 2nd Appellate Court, this question too stands
answered against the appellant.

9
19. Consequently, no substantial question of law as
framed by the Court on 21st December, 2004, is called for
determination by the Second Appellate Court, hence, the Second
Appeal fails and is accordingly dismissed.
20. There would be no order as to costs.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
